etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French qualifier (“to qualify”). Equivalent to quality +‎ -fy.

definitions.definition: To describe or characterize something by listing its qualities.

quote.citation: 1999, Matthew C. Bagger, Religious Experience, Justification, and History, →ISBN, page 62:
quote.text: Descartes's methodism with its regulative criterion leads him to explicitly deny that accidentally true belief qualifies as knowledge.

quote.citation: 2007 February 11, Jay Romano, “Triggering a Rent Increase”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: But if it is done in conjunction with repointing of the building, the work would probably qualify as a major capital improvement.

definitions.definition: To make someone, or to become competent or eligible for some position or task.

quote.citation: 1856 December, [Thomas Babington] Macaulay, “Samuel Johnson”, in T[homas] F[lower] E[llis], editor, The Miscellaneous Writings and Speeches of Lord Macaulay, new edition, London: Longman, Green, Reader, & Dyer, published 1871, →OCLC:
quote.text: He had qualified himself for municipal office by taking the oaths to the sovereigns in possession.
Wales claimed their first points in Euro 2012 qualifying with a morale-boosting victory in Cardiff over former Group G joint leaders Montenegro.

definitions.definition: To certify or license someone for something.
To modify, limit, restrict or moderate something; especially to add conditions or requirements for an assertion to be true.

quote.citation: 1609, William Shakespeare, “Sonnet 109”, in Shake-speares Sonnets. […], London: By G[eorge] Eld for T[homas] T[horpe] and are to be sold by William Aspley, →OCLC:
quote.text: O! never say that I was false of heart,Though absence seem'd my flame to qualify

definitions.definition: (now rare) To mitigate, alleviate (something); to make less disagreeable.

quote.citation: 1590, Edmund Spenser, “Book II, Canto VI”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London:  […]  [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:
quote.text: he balmes and herbes thereto applyde, / And euermore with mighty spels them charmd, / That in short space he has them qualifyde, / And him restor'd to health, that would haue algates dyde.

definitions.definition: To compete successfully in some stage of a competition and become eligible for the next stage.
To give individual quality to; to modulate; to vary; to regulate.

quote.citation: 1650, Thomas Browne, Pseudodoxia Epidemica: […], 2nd edition, London:  […]  A[braham] Miller, for Edw[ard] Dod and Nath[aniel] Ekins, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: It hath no larynx  […]  to qualify the sound.

definitions.definition: (juggling) To throw and catch each object at least twice.
(juggling) An instance of throwing and catching each prop at least twice.
